details: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) for June 2026 revealed headline inflation falling to 3.5% year-over-year, below the anticipated 3.8%. Core CPI, excluding volatile food and energy, also came in lower at 2.6% year-over-year. This unexpected moderation in inflation has significantly reduced the likelihood of aggressive Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, leading to a broad rebound in risk assets, including Bitcoin and Ethereum. Crypto markets reacted positively to the news, with Bitcoin reclaiming key price levels.
title: US Inflation Cools More Than Expected, Boosting Crypto Outlook

details: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, in his testimony on July 14, 2026, reinforced the central bank's commitment to combating inflation, stating that the Fed has "no tolerance for persistently high inflation." He emphasized that monetary policy determines underlying inflation. While cooler CPI data was released the same day, Warsh's hawkish stance suggests the Fed remains cautious, potentially tempering expectations for rapid monetary easing.
title: Fed Chair Warsh Reiterates Vigilance Against Persistent Inflation

details: The U.S. House of Representatives passed the "21st Century ROAD to Housing Act," which notably includes a provision that prohibits the issuance of a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) by the United States through December 31, 2030. This legislative action signals a preference for decentralized digital assets over a government-issued digital currency for the foreseeable future in the U.S.
title: US House Passes Bill Prohibiting Central Bank Digital Currency Until 2030

details: Escalating geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran have driven global oil prices higher, with WTI crude surpassing $80 a barrel. This increase in energy costs raises concerns about a potential rebound in inflation, which could lead the Federal Reserve to maintain a more restrictive monetary policy. Such a scenario could put renewed pressure on risk assets, including Bitcoin.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Escalate, Oil Prices Rise, Weighing on Bitcoin

details: Despite recent price movements, spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) continued to experience significant net outflows. On July 14, 2026, these ETFs recorded over $424.66 million in net outflows, ending a modest inflow streak from the previous week. This trend indicates a persistent cautious sentiment among institutional investors regarding the Bitcoin asset class.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Continued Outflows Amid Broader Market Pressure
